analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing (Nov 3, 2026)
key_insights: JPM US Market Intel stays Tactically Bullish on SPX and updates its Monetization Menu (Nov 2): a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals weighted toward Cyclicals, with Consumers and Financials favored if the curve keeps steepening.

Positioning Intel finds that when the NDX is within about 6% of its all-time high and falls 3.5% or more, it rebounds about 3% the following week. The effect is stronger when the decline happens on a Friday, which points to de-grossing rather than a change in fundamentals.

JPM argues AI capex cuts would not trigger a recession. Reasons: record household net worth and cash, record or near-record corporate margins, and AI is not a significant driver of hiring. The larger effects would be lower capex (a GDP drag) and possible hyperscaler layoffs.

The biggest non-AI risk is a re-escalation in the Middle East. JPM says oil already appears to price another round of attacks, which limits upside for energy prices, bond yields and downside for equities.
Seasonality is a tailwind: November has been the strongest month on average this century, and post-midterm seasonality is also positive.
Equity derivatives price about a 90bp move around the US midterm elections, similar to what is priced for NFP in a normal week.
Stocks closed higher in a quiet session into election results. AI fears are tied to the Texas gubernatorial outcome: a GOP win is bullish for tech and a Democratic win is bearish.

JOLTS for September was uniformly slightly better: openings rate 4.5% from 4.3%, hires 3.4% from 3.3%, quits 2.1% from 1.9% (best since June 2025), layoffs 1.0% from 1.1%. This supports JPM's forecast that compensation growth levels off soon.

Europe closed lower (UKX -1.1%, SX5E -0.5%, SXXP -0.6%, DAX -0.4%) with yields materially higher as curves bear steepened. Earnings drove trading and investors are not pre-positioning for the midterms.
ETF desk flows ahead of the midterms: customers are selling crypto-exposed equities and IBIT (linked to the Binance hack), and buying India (INDY/INDA) and Japan (EWJ/FLJP).
Delta-One Factors sees pre-election sentiment as overhyped. A likely reversal would see tech (XLK) outperform healthcare (XLV), with further upside for Momentum, Beta and AI factor trades.
Energy desk notes that oil moved against the consensus direction the Monday after both Midnight Hammer and Maduro's capture, and net Brent positioning is about the same as before Midnight Hammer.

AMD earnings setup: the buyside bar for the 4Q revenue guide is $16.87B, investors expect a guide between $16.2B and about $17B, and shorts have risen materially. INTC's weak guide raises doubts about the PC client business, about 25% of AMD revenue.
Tomorrow's US calendar: ADP, Treasury Quarterly Refunding, trade balance, S&P Global PMI services and ISM services. Earnings include UBER, MCD, DDOG, CVS, QCOM, APP and SNAP.

market_movers.rationale: Investors view the revenue guide as high and the stock as expensive, and shorts have risen. INTC's weak guide raises risk to the client business, about 25% of AMD revenue.

sector_views.rationale: JPM would not abandon the Tech trade and plays for a tactical rebound, but expects the market to become more selective between AI winners and losers.
A heavier weight on Cyclicals in the Tech and Cyclicals barbell, particularly if the yield curve continues to steepen.
Delta-One Factors expects tech to outperform healthcare if pre-election sentiment reverses.

earnings_insights: AMD (reports 11/3 after close): JPM TMT's buyside bar for the 4Q revenue guide is $16.87B (an investor expectation, not consensus). Investors who shared numbers expect a guide of $16.2B to about $17B, above the unmoved Street consensus. A gross margin guide of 55.5% or higher is widely expected.
AMD: most survey respondents do not expect an update to the guide for server CPU revenue to grow 70% in 2027 or for data center revenue to more than double.
INTC's weak guide (already reported) raises the question of whether PC slowdown and OEM order weakness is idiosyncratic. Client is about 25% of AMD revenue.
Earnings macro read-through from the briefing summary: mixed signals on the labor market (wage inflation, headcount reduction, skilled labor shortages) and bullish comments on AI infrastructure.

risk_factors: Re-escalation in the Middle East is the biggest non-AI risk.
AI headlines on capital raising, circular financing and legal issues may give investors pause.
AI capex declines could hit GDP growth and cause hyperscaler layoffs.
INTC's weak guide may signal a broader PC slowdown that reaches AMD.
Non-USD AI debt offerings may affect the broader EU bond market.
Election outcome risk, including the Texas gubernatorial result, which JPM ties to AI sentiment.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 16.91 in one afternoon update and 20.83 in the other.
Equity derivatives price about a 90bp move around the midterm elections, similar to NFP in a normal week.
Net Brent positioning is about the same as before Midnight Hammer, roughly 30m barrels less.
Shorts in AMD have risen materially over the past week.
Positioning Intel attributes Friday's NDX flush to likely de-grossing.
geopolitical: US midterm elections on Nov 3 with poll closings from 7pm to 1am ET.
US/Iran headlines: a deal was thought agreed and later refuted. A WSJ article describes considerable damage to US regional bases by Iran.
JPM sees depleted munitions limiting another wave of US attacks, which may point to heightened diplomatic efforts.
US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027.
APEC Leaders Meeting Nov 18-19 in Shenzhen, G20 Summit Dec 15-16 in Miami, US government funding deadline Dec 11.

tension_points.bull_case: Delta-One Factors says pre-election sentiment is overhyped, and a reversal once policy implementation begins would favor tech over healthcare and lift Momentum, Beta and AI trades.
tension_points.bear_case: Delta-One Thematics says midterms may be priced but gridlock is not, with policy asymmetries under a gridlocked Washington. AI fears are tied to the Texas gubernatorial result, where a Democratic win is bearish.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Democratic victory in the Texas Gubernatorial election, which the report calls bearish for tech.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM Market Intel argues consumers have record net worth and cash, corporate margins are at or near records, and AI is not a significant driver of hiring.
tension_points.bear_case: Weekend AI headlines on capital raising, circular financing and legal issues, and the turmoil around CRWV, raise questions about AI monetization and a possible domino effect.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Corporate margin compression, which the report says would need to occur before mass layoffs begin.

tension_points.bull_case: Channel checks suggest a solid quarter and a good guide, with AMD more insulated than INTC through product management, TSMC flexibility and less enterprise exposure in Client.
tension_points.bear_case: Revenue guide looks high, the stock looks expensive, shorts are up, and INTC's weak guide may reflect a broader PC slowdown. Client is about 25% of revenue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An AMD guide below the $16.87B buyside bar, with downside toward $16.2B.
